intro.text: Every software project travels through the same seven phases. Think of a relay race, where each phase hands something to the next.

plan.text: Planning comes first. The goal is a plan for the whole project. Its output is the Software Project Management Plan: the S P M P.

analysis.text: Requirements analysis defines what to build. Its output is the Software Requirements Specification: the S R S.

design.text: Design describes how to build it. Its output is the Software Design Document: the S D D.

dev.text: Development turns the design into program code, and integrates the parts.

unit.text: Testing checks that code, level by level. Unit tests check single modules. Integration tests check that modules work together.

regress.text: Regression tests check that a new change broke nothing old. System tests check the whole system against the user requirements.

users.text: Then the users. Beta testing is real-world use by the users. Acceptance testing is done by the project owner, to decide if the product is ready for release.

deploy.text: Deployment puts the product into production. Its outputs: the delivered system, a release description, and trained users.

maint.text: Maintenance keeps going after the release. It fixes defects, adds enhancements, and improves things like performance and reliability.

recap.text: Remember the three documents. S P M P from planning. S R S from analysis. S D D from design.
